claims: Robert Mueller was subpoenaed by the House Oversight Committee in August 2025 regarding the Justice Department's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case.
The subpoena was withdrawn due to Robert Mueller's health, specifically a Parkinson's disease diagnosis.
Rep. James Comer is chairman of the House Oversight Committee.
Rep. James Comer issued the subpoena to Robert Mueller to testify regarding the long-term investigation into Epstein.
The House Oversight Committee withdrew the subpoena after learning of Robert Mueller's health issues.
Mueller’s family disclosed in August 2025 that Robert Mueller was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the summer of 2021.
The long-term investigation into Epstein focused on the 2008 non-prosecution agreement that allowed Epstein to plead guilty to state charges in Florida.
Robert Mueller was the FBI director from 2001 to 2013.
In documents related to Epstein released by the DOJ, Mueller's name appeared in communications from 2017 to 2018 where Epstein discussed the Russia probe with associates.
Robert Mueller died at the age of 81.
